scenarios.title: Falling object
scenarios.description: Something dropped or thrown straight up or down: a skydiver, a ball, a raindrop.
scenarios.law: Newton's second law along the vertical: mass times acceleration equals weight plus the other forces.

effects.label: Air resistance
effects.description: A force opposing the motion that grows with speed.

effects.label: Buoyancy
effects.description: The surrounding fluid pushes up with the weight of the fluid displaced.

effects.label: Gravity weakens with height
effects.description: Inverse-square gravity, for very high drops.

presets.label: Skydiver
presets.description: An 80 kg skydiver, belly to earth, jumping from 4000 m.

presets.label: Dropped baseball
presets.description: A baseball dropped from a 50 m tower; where is it after 2 s?

presets.label: Ball thrown upward
presets.description: A ball thrown up at 20 m/s from a 1.5 m hand, no air resistance.

presets.label: Raindrop
presets.description: A raindrop is seen to fall at 6.5 m/s: what is its drag coefficient c?

presets.label: Fog droplet
presets.description: A 20 µm droplet, slow enough for linear (Stokes) drag.

scenarios.title: Projectile
scenarios.description: Something launched at an angle: a kicked ball, a golf drive, a basketball shot.
scenarios.law: Newton's second law in two directions: gravity acts downward, and air resistance (if any) opposes the velocity.

effects.label: Air resistance
effects.description: A force opposing the velocity through the air.

effects.label: Wind
effects.description: A steady horizontal wind; it only matters when there is air resistance.

presets.label: Free kick
presets.description: A ball kicked at 25 m/s, 30° above the ground, ignoring the air.

presets.label: Golf drive
presets.description: A 45.9 g golf ball driven at 70 m/s and 12°, with air resistance.

presets.label: Basketball free throw
presets.description: Released 2.1 m up at 7.3 m/s; the hoop is 4.19 m away and 3.05 m high. What angle?

presets.label: Long jump
presets.description: A jumper leaves the board at 9.5 m/s and lands 8.0 m away: what take-off angle?

presets.label: Javelin in a headwind
presets.description: An 800 g javelin thrown at 28 m/s and 36° from 1.8 m into a 5 m/s headwind.

scenarios.title: Mass on a spring
scenarios.description: Anything that bounces on a spring: a car on its suspension, a door closer, a lab cart.
scenarios.law: Newton's second law with Hooke's law: the spring pulls back in proportion to the stretch.

effects.label: Damping
effects.description: A friction force proportional to speed (a shock absorber).

effects.label: Gravity (vertical spring)
effects.description: The weight stretches the spring to a new rest position.

presets.label: Car suspension
presets.description: One corner of a car (400 kg) pushed down 5 cm and released: where is it after 0.3 s?

presets.label: Door closer
presets.description: What damping makes a 30 kg door on a 60 N/m closer shut without bouncing (ζ = 1)?

presets.label: Lab cart
presets.description: A cart on a spring is timed at 1.0 s per swing: what is the spring constant?

presets.label: Washing machine
presets.description: A 60 kg drum on its mounts, shaken by an unbalanced load at 5 Hz.

presets.label: Hanging scale
presets.description: A 2 kg bag stretches a spring scale 4 cm: what is k, and how fast does it bob?

scenarios.title: Pendulum
scenarios.description: A weight swinging on a string or rod: a clock pendulum, a playground swing, a wrecking ball.
scenarios.law: Newton's second law for rotation: the component of gravity along the arc pulls the bob back towards the bottom.

effects.label: Large swings
effects.description: Keep sin θ instead of approximating it by θ (needed beyond about 15°).

effects.label: Damping
effects.description: Air resistance and friction at the pivot, proportional to angular velocity.

presets.label: Grandfather clock
presets.description: A clock pendulum must tick once a second (period 2 s): how long is it?

presets.label: Playground swing
presets.description: A 2.5 m swing pulled back 60° and released.

presets.label: Foucault pendulum
presets.description: The 67 m pendulum in the Panthéon, released from 3°.

presets.label: Damped lab pendulum
presets.description: A 0.5 m pendulum released from 10° with damping rate 0.1 per second: its angle after 10 s.

presets.label: Measuring gravity
presets.description: A 1.000 m pendulum takes 2.007 s per swing: what is g there?

scenarios.title: Cooling and heating
scenarios.description: An object settling to the temperature of its surroundings: coffee cooling, a roast heating, a body after death.
scenarios.law: Newton's law of cooling: the temperature changes at a rate proportional to its difference from the surroundings.

fields.label: Time for the difference to halve

effects.label: Heat source
effects.description: A heater (or the object's own heat) warming it at a steady rate.

presets.label: Cooling coffee
presets.description: Coffee at 90 °C in a 22 °C room is 75 °C after 5 minutes: when is it 60 °C?

presets.label: Time since death
presets.description: A body at 29.5 °C in an 18 °C room, cooling constant 0.19 per hour.

presets.label: Roast in the oven
presets.description: A 5 °C roast in a 180 °C oven reaches 40 °C in 30 min: when is it 70 °C?

presets.label: Processor warming up
presets.description: A chip in 25 °C air heats at 3 °C/s with cooling constant 0.05 per second.

scenarios.title: Exponential decay and growth
scenarios.description: A quantity that changes in proportion to itself: radioactive decay, a drug leaving the body, bacteria multiplying.
scenarios.law: The rate of change is proportional to the amount present.

effects.label: Direction
effects.description: Whether the amount shrinks or grows.

presets.label: Carbon dating
presets.description: A bone has 25% of its original carbon-14 (half-life 5730 years): how old is it?

presets.label: Iodine-131 dose
presets.description: 400 MBq of iodine-131 (half-life 8.02 days): how much is left after 30 days?

presets.label: Drug elimination
presets.description: A 200 mg dose is down to 150 mg after 2 hours: what is left after 12 hours?

presets.label: Bacteria doubling
presets.description: 1000 bacteria doubling every 20 minutes: when are there a million?

scenarios.title: RC circuit
scenarios.description: A capacitor charging or discharging through a resistor: a camera flash, a timer, a filter.
scenarios.law: Kirchhoff's voltage law around the loop: the source voltage equals the resistor drop plus the capacitor voltage.

effects.label: Internal resistance
effects.description: A real source has some resistance of its own, in series.

effects.label: Leaky capacitor
effects.description: A real capacitor slowly leaks through a large parallel resistance.

presets.label: Camera flash
presets.description: A 120 µF flash capacitor charging to 300 V through 2 kΩ: when is it at 285 V (95%)?

presets.label: Timing circuit
presets.description: A 5 V timer: how long until the capacitor reaches 3.3 V?

presets.label: Touch sensor
presets.description: A touch pad charges to 2.0 V in 110 µs through 1 MΩ from 3.3 V: what is its capacitance?

presets.label: Defibrillator
presets.description: A 32 µF capacitor at 5 kV discharging through a 50 Ω chest: the state after 2 ms.

presets.label: Audio low-pass filter
presets.description: A 1 kΩ, 100 nF filter fed with a 5 kHz tone.

scenarios.title: RL circuit
scenarios.description: A coil and a resistor: a relay, a motor winding, an electromagnet switching on or off.
scenarios.law: Kirchhoff's voltage law: the source voltage equals the resistor drop plus the inductor's back-EMF, L di/dt.

effects.label: Internal resistance
effects.description: A real source has some resistance of its own, in series.

presets.label: Relay coil
presets.description: A 12 V relay (200 mH, 240 Ω) pulls in at 35 mA: how long after switch-on?

presets.label: Electromagnet
presets.description: A 2 H lifting magnet with 4 Ω on 48 V: final current and stored energy.

presets.label: Coil switched off
presets.description: A coil carrying 3 A is shorted through 15 Ω and falls to 1 A in 2 ms: what is L?

presets.label: Motor winding on AC
presets.description: A 50 mH, 10 Ω winding on a 325 V, 50 Hz supply.
